call.note: the callee at 0x4f04f30 IS an FDE start (144 bytes, .eh_frame+0x00282318, CIE 0x00000000, the same CIE as the window), but its body is excluded here; only the call encoding and the FDE record are retained, so no claim about what it computes is made

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, no runtime rebase

function.padding_note: two int3 bytes (0xcc) at [0x4f0510e, 0x4f05110) pad the window to the next FDE at 0x4f05110

validated_caller_fdes.note: the caller disassembly from its FDE start shows the e8 call to the window at 0x4f04a37 as an instruction start, and the caller then compares the window return against the sentinel 0x8000000000000001 (movabs rcx, sentinel; cmp rcx, rax; jne), so the sentinel convention is consumed by a verified caller; the caller role beyond that check is not established

edges.note: ordinary clamp: requested 5 with old capacity 10 gives min(6, 20) = 6, above the floor; flag set, so the window returns the (out+8, out+16) pair
upper clamp binds: requested 100 with old capacity 10 gives min(101, 20) = 20; flag set, so the window returns the pair
flag clear: requested 5 with old capacity 10 gives newcap 6, the window stores newcap into the struct capacity field and out+8 into the struct pointer field, and returns the sentinel
floor binds: old capacity 0 with requested 0 gives min(1, 0) = 0, floored to 4; flag clear, so the window stores 4 and returns the sentinel
floor binds on the pair path: old capacity 1 with requested 100 gives min(101, 2) = 2, floored to 4; flag set, so the window returns the pair with newcap 4
floor boundary, upper side: old capacity 3 with requested 4 gives min(5, 6) = 5, so the cmovae floor does not change the value; flag set, pair returned
floor boundary, lower side: old capacity 3 with requested 3 gives min(4, 6) = 4, equal to the floor either way; flag set, pair returned
floor binds below the boundary: old capacity 3 with requested 2 gives min(3, 6) = 3, floored to 4; flag set, pair returned
upper-clamp wrap: old capacity 2^64-1 doubles to 2^64-2 mod 2^64, requested 0 gives min(1, 2^64-2) = 1, floored to 4; flag clear, sentinel plus store
request wrap: requested 2^64-1 increments to 0 mod 2^64, min(0, 2*old) = 0, floored to 4; flag set, pair returned with newcap 4
upper-clamp equality: requested 19 with old capacity 10 gives requested+1 = 20 exactly equal to twice the old capacity, so the cmovbe upper clamp leaves the value at 20; flag set, pair returned

rule.formula: newcap = max(4, min((requested + 1) mod 2^64, (2 * oldcap) mod 2^64)); call 0x4f04f30 with rdi = stack out-struct at [rbp-0x28], rsi = oldcap, rdx = oldptr, rcx = newcap; if the callee-set flag byte at out+0 is 0, store newcap into the struct capacity field and out+8 into the struct pointer field and return 0x8000000000000001; else return rax = out+8 and rdx = out+16
rule.formula_note: the clamp is unsigned: cmovbe takes the minimum of requested+1 and twice the old capacity, and cmovae keeps the minimum only when it is at least 5, else the floor 4. The flag byte is the callee output at out+0; what makes the callee set or clear it is excluded with the callee body. On the flag-clear path the window does not set rdx, so rdx after a sentinel return is not determined by this window bytes alone. On the flag-set path the window returns the (out+8, out+16) pair in rax:rdx without storing into the struct. The single verified caller stores its rsi into the struct capacity field before the call, so for that caller oldcap equals requested at entry and the formula reduces to requested+1 floored to 4; that reduction is caller context, not the general rule.
rule.inputs: struct pointer (rdi; capacity qword at +0, pointer qword at +8), requested count (rsi), old capacity (the qword at [rdi]), old pointer (the qword at [rdi+8]), callee outputs (flag byte at out+0, qword at out+8, qword at out+16)
